frozenBefore: any pilot-v2 training run was started
gateSetPolicy: The eligibility gates are reused UNCHANGED from pilot v1. Pilot v1 failed on guitarSetRootRegression; a v2 that moved that gate would be answering its own question. The gate file is not edited by this pilot.

predecessor.measuredFailure: mixed-domain-finetune passed every full-band gate (+14.83 pp full-mix detailed, +0.135 no-chord F1) and failed only GuitarSet root preservation: 4.8 pp on audio_mono-mic and 8.18 pp on audio_mono-pickup_mix against a 2.0 pp tolerance.

strategy.description: Keep the pilot-v1 strategy (fine-tune v1 on GuitarSet rehearsal batches mixed with Slakh full-band batches, four exported heads unchanged) and add exactly one preservation mechanism per candidate, so the mechanism that recovers GuitarSet root accuracy is identifiable rather than inferred.
rationale: Measured in pilot v1: the failure is specific to root identification. GuitarSet detailed accuracy did NOT regress (-1.54 pp microphone, +0.57 pp pickup, both inside tolerance) and fragmentation improved on both captures (-0.0237, -0.1017). Only root accuracy fell. A general-purpose stability intervention would therefore be aimed at the wrong quantity.

Measured in pilot v1: the guitarset-only control gained just +1.69 pp on the full mix against the primary's +14.83 pp, so the full-band capability comes from full-band exposure. Any v2 candidate must keep that exposure rather than trade it away for preservation.

Measured in pilot v1: the primary's best epoch was 11 of a frozen 12-epoch budget, so its full-band figures are a lower bound and the schedule is kept identical rather than extended - extending it would confound preservation with convergence.

Capability and preservation are both required by the frozen gate set, so the question is not whether full-band training helps (it does, measurably) but whether the resulting root forgetting can be prevented at acceptable full-band cost.

rejectedAlternatives.reason: The gate was frozen before any full-band result existed, precisely so that a model which forgets solo guitar could not be argued into eligibility afterwards. Pilot v1 missed it by 4.8 and 8.18 pp, which is not a boundary case.

The full-band gain is a representation-level change (the control, which optimised the same heads without full-band audio, gained almost nothing). Freezing the trunk would remove the mechanism that produced the +14.83 pp.

Requires a Fisher estimate over the v1 training distribution and adds a second untuned hyperparameter. Root-head distillation anchors the same quantity the gate measures, directly and with one weight.
The v1 primary was still improving at the budget end. Training longer would change capability and preservation simultaneously and make the v2 comparison unreadable.

domainSampling.note: Default inherited from pilot v1. Candidates may override it; each override is recorded on the candidate and reported.
domainSampling.slakhViewNote: Unchanged from pilot v1. Guitar-only views measured worse than the full mix for every engine.

sharedSchedule.seedNote: Deliberately the same seed as pilot v1. The two candidates that keep the 50/50 ratio then see the exact same epoch stream v1's primary saw, so their difference against it is the intervention alone and not a different draw.

candidates.note: The direct dial on the failing gate. The epoch mixer sizes an epoch by the domain that can supply its share without repetition, so at 0.7/0.3 it still draws all 240 Slakh samples - exactly as many as the 50/50 v1 primary did - while GuitarSet rises from 240 to 560 samples per epoch. Full-band exposure per epoch is therefore identical to v1's and only rehearsal changes.
candidates.predictedFailureMode: If root accuracy is recovered only by diluting the full-band signal, the full-band detailed improvement will fall below the 2.0 pp gate and this candidate fails the other half.

preservation.note: KL(teacher || student) over the root posterior, averaged over unpadded rehearsal-domain frames only, added to the frozen v1 objective. Slakh frames are unconstrained, so the anchor cannot suppress full-band learning directly.
preservation.headsNote: Root only. Pilot v1 measured the regression as specific to root: detailed accuracy and fragmentation both stayed inside tolerance, so anchoring the other heads would constrain quantities that are not failing.
preservation.weightNote: Frozen at 1.0 and NOT tuned. There is no held-out budget to tune it on and tuning it against the Slakh development set would leak selection into the dev metric. 1.0 is the least-assumption choice against a root cross-entropy of comparable scale.

candidates.note: Same 50/50 stream and schedule as the v1 primary, plus an explicit anchor on the quantity the gate measures. Isolates 'anchor the root posterior' from 'see less full-band audio'.

Same 50/50 stream as the v1 primary at 0.4x the step size. Separates 'this intervention preserved root accuracy' from 'any smaller step would have'. Without it, a rehearsal-heavy or distilled win could not be distinguished from simply drifting less.
candidates.predictedFailureMode: Likely trades capability for preservation symmetrically - less drift in both directions - and misses the 2.0 pp full-band improvement gate. That outcome is informative and is why it is an ablation rather than a candidate for promotion.

referenceResults.note: Pilot v1 numbers are NOT recomputed. They were produced by this same evaluator against this same gate set and are cited directly for comparison.

deviationFromGateSetCpuPolicy.justification: The gate-set CPU policy was written from an ESTIMATED cost of 7.97 hours for the pilot. The measured cost of pilot v1 was 35.7 minutes for both candidates combined (1162.8 s primary, 91.0 s control). The stated rationale for the one-candidate bound - that a broader search is not affordable - is measurably false at this scale, so the bound is widened deliberately and recorded here rather than exceeded silently.
deviationFromGateSetCpuPolicy.unchanged: This deviation touches the CPU budget only. No eligibility gate, threshold, split, sealed performer or reporting requirement is altered.

evaluation.fullBandDevelopment: Slakh validation split only; the untouched test split is never used for selection.
evaluation.guitarSetPreservation: p01-p05 development metrics, both captures; p00 stays sealed.

knownLimitations: Reference labels are note-level (~0.6 s mean region, ~100 regions/minute vs ~20 for GuitarSet human annotations), so the frozen full-band fragmentation gate cannot honestly be applied to them and is reported as not-evaluable rather than passed.
The percussion-only control is scored against harmonic labels rather than an all-no-chord reference, so the frozen noChordRecallMinimum gate cannot be evaluated as written.

GuitarSet preservation is measured on p01-p05, which v1 was already trained on and which every candidate rehearses. It is a catastrophic-forgetting check on data v1 already knew, not a held-out generalisation claim.
Slakh2100 is rendered from MIDI. Even a fully passing pilot is synthetic-domain evidence and does not establish production readiness.
The distillation weight is frozen untuned, so a null result for root-anchored-distillation bounds that mechanism at weight 1.0 rather than refuting the mechanism itself.
